name: Exception Handling Fundamentals
overview: Break a tiny Java program on purpose. Follow the exception up the call stack and find the first place that can actually do something about it.

sections.title: Know when the failure happens
sections.content: The compiler catches invalid source. During execution, a problem such as accessing past the end of an array can throw an exception object.

sections.title: Follow the stack
sections.content: Java searches for a matching catch handler in the current method and its callers. If no handler catches the exception, the affected thread ends.

images.caption: The JVM looks for a matching handler as the call stack unwinds.

sections.title: Recover where you can
sections.content: Handle a specific failure where you can give a useful response or retry safely. Let other failures propagate to a caller that has more context.

codeExamples.title: Runtime Error Example
codeExamples.code:
int[] arr = new int[2];
arr[5] = 10; // runtime exception

keyPoints: Trace a divide-by-zero failure from the crash site to a handler. You've got it when you can explain where to recover and where to let it propagate.

interviewQA.question: What happens after a method throws?
interviewQA.answer: Normal execution in that method stops. Java looks for a matching handler as it unwinds the stack.

interviewQA.question: Does an uncaught exception always stop the whole JVM?
interviewQA.answer: It ends the affected thread. Other threads can keep running.
